title: DO WELL · Opportunity to completion
runtime: Live Do Well Android app · hosted backend · two accounts

chapters.narration: Five point nine million Filipinos. Employed, and still looking for more work. That was August 2026, according to the Philippine Statistics Authority. Unemployment eased from July, but it is still higher than a year ago. People want to work. The question is: can they find it?

chapters.narration: Underemployment means a person is employed, but wants more hours, another job, or a job with longer hours. In August, that described eleven point nine percent of employed Filipinos. Unemployment was five point three percent: lower than July, but higher than August last year. These are different measures. Together, they show why access to suitable work matters.

chapters.narration: Think of a student who wants a few paid hours around class, or someone already working who needs more. On the other side, a small café needs extra hands for one busy weekend. Both sides face the same three questions. Where is the right work? What exactly needs to be done? And how do both people know the job is finished?

chapters.narration: This is Do Well. Find nearby work. Get it done well. A native Android app for short-term local and remote gigs, running on a live cloud backend. Meet Maya, who runs a café in Makati, and Alex, a student looking for extra work. Everything you are about to see is the real app.

beats.title: DO WELL
beats.body: Find nearby work. Get it done well.

beats.title:
Maya posts.
Alex delivers.
beats.body: Two accounts. One live marketplace.

chapters.narration: Maya needs help setting up a weekend community event. Instead of a vague post, she opens the Job Brief Builder. She describes the task in one sentence, then picks a category, the work mode, a general area and her budget. The builder turns that into a structured brief: a clear title, the scope, step by step tasks with acceptance criteria, and safety notes. Maya applies it to the form, sets the title and her six hundred peso offer, and publishes. Within seconds, the gig is live. Every field stays editable before it goes live.

chapters.narration: Now Alex. His home screen lists open gigs, with filters for on site and remote work. Location is optional. When Alex looks for nearby work, Android shows its own permission prompt, and Do Well asks only for approximate location, while the app is in use. There is no background tracking, and exact addresses are never shared. Alex can also skip GPS entirely, and pick a Metro Manila hub and a search radius. Every result shows a rounded distance and a plain reason why it fits.

chapters.narration: Alex opens the café gig. He sees the pay, the general area, and the full brief. Meeting details are agreed directly with the employer, never posted publicly. He applies with a short note that only Maya can read, and the application appears in his work list right away. If his plans change, he can withdraw it.

beats.body: Applied · pending review

chapters.narration: On Maya's phone, the Activity feed reports a new application. She turns on device alerts, and Android asks for notification permission at the moment it is useful, not at launch. Maya reads Alex's note and selects him. Do Well explains exactly what happens next: the listing closes, other pending applications are declined, and an agreement is proposed. Nothing is final until Alex accepts.

chapters.narration: Alex sees the update in his own Activity feed. He opens the task agreement, reviews the terms and the agreed amount, and accepts. The agreement is now active. Maya then breaks the job into milestones: arranging tables and chairs, setting out supplies, and tidying up afterwards. Both of them now share one checklist, so expectations are clear before the work begins.

chapters.narration: On Saturday, Alex starts each milestone, so Maya can follow the progress. When the work is done, he writes a completion note. He can attach up to three photos from the gallery or the camera, and Android asks for camera access only when he taps. Then he submits the work for review.

chapters.narration: Maya's phone lights up with Android notifications: the agreement confirmed, each milestone started, and the work submitted. She opens the submission, reads Alex's note, and approves it. She could also request a revision. All three milestones are marked approved, and the task agreement is complete. The completed agreement keeps a record of the six hundred pesos they agreed on.

chapters.narration: Do Well is built for the way Android phones are really used. Connections drop, so the app watches network state. When Alex goes offline, it switches to a saved snapshot and says so clearly, then refreshes once he reconnects. Permissions are requested in context and kept to a minimum. And when Maya approves, Alex gets his own notification, and the job moves to completed in his work list and profile.

chapters.narration: So what makes Do Well different? A structured brief instead of a vague post. Discovery that explains itself. An agreement both sides confirm, milestones both can see, and a clear finish. For judging, that means innovation in the workflow, a native Android experience, privacy first security, complete functionality, and a calm, consistent user experience.

beats.title:
One connection.
A complete workflow.
beats.body: Brief → Discover → Apply → Agree → Deliver → Approve
